# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 22 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 22 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_022_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 22

**22:1** Now Herod was searching for John, and he sent officers to Zechariah at the altar, saying: "Where have you hidden your son?" And Zechariah answered them: "I am a minister of God and serve at his temple. I do not know where my son is."

**22:2** And the officers departed and reported everything to Herod. And Herod was angry and said: "His son is to become king of Israel." And he sent to Zechariah again, saying: "Tell the truth: where is your son? Know that your blood is under my hand." And the officers went and delivered the message to him.

**22:3** And Zechariah said: "I am a martyr of God. Take my blood. But the Lord will receive my spirit, for you will shed innocent blood at the entrance of the temple of the Lord."

**22:4** And toward the break of dawn Zechariah was slain. And the children of Israel did not know that he had been slain.

---

## Translator's Note

Zechariah's murder at the temple altar (22:3-4) is the Protevangelium's interpretation of Jesus's reference to "the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah" in Matthew 23:35 and Luke 11:51. The text makes Zechariah a proto-martyr: his declaration "I am a martyr of God" (*martys Theou eimi*) uses the Greek word *martys* in its early Christian sense of "witness who suffers death." This is one of the earliest explicit uses of "martyr" in a technical sense. Zechariah's defiance — "Take my blood, but the Lord will receive my spirit" — is deliberately patterned on Stephen's martyrdom (Acts 7:59).
